content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT NEEDS FOR {{SURVIVAL}} MODE
facts: **Hydrate before coffee** – drink 1 full glass of water before your first cup, since sleep deprivation already leaves you dehydrated and caffeine will make it worse.
**Batch protein snacks** – prep boiled eggs or turkey slices in bulk so you grab protein instead of sugar during 3am feeds.
**Nap when baby naps, once a day minimum** – even 20 minutes lowers cortisol enough to protect your immune system through the newborn stretch.
**Skip the scale for 6 weeks** – your body is rebuilding tissue and blood volume, not just losing fat, so early weigh-ins mostly cause stress with no useful info.
**Split night shifts with a partner if possible** – alternating 4-hour blocks of uninterrupted sleep restores more function than both parents getting broken sleep all night.
**Keep a water bottle at every feeding spot** – breastfeeding alone can pull an extra 25-32 oz of fluid a day, so refill spots matter more than willpower.
**Eat something within 30 minutes of waking**, even if it's small, to stop the blood sugar crash that makes new-parent exhaustion feel worse than it is.
**Ask for one specific task from visitors** – 'bring dinner Tuesday' gets help; 'let me know if you need anything' rarely does.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
New parent life runs on a few small, repeatable moves. Hydrate before coffee matters more than people think — after broken sleep your body is already running low on fluid, and caffeine is a mild diuretic, so pairing it with water first keeps your energy from crashing an hour later. Batch protein snacks work because steady protein keeps blood sugar from spiking and dropping, which is exactly what makes exhaustion feel unbearable during nighttime feeds. And skipping the scale for 6 weeks isn't just a mood thing — your blood volume, fluid retention, and uterus are all still shifting back, so an early number on a scale doesn't reflect what's actually happening inside your body. Everyone's recovery timeline is different, listen to yours.
